article_title: Vogue’s A to Z wedding directory will fully prep you for your special day
sub_title: The one-size-fits-all kind of wedding is a thing of the past. Let this A-Z directory be your guide for crafting a celebration that is authentic to you
article_content: The era of cookie-cutter weddings is over. Today, it’s all about creating a celebration that feels like it was designed for you from start to finish. Whether you’re dreaming of an intimate garden soirée or a three-day destination spectacle, the possibilities are as limitless as your imagination. To help you navigate it all, we’ve put together an A to Z wedding directory covering everything that injects personality into your nuptials. Think of it as your blueprint for a wedding that is equal parts stylish, personal and unforgettable. From handwoven textiles to locally-sourced seasonal Bachelorette trips are trading late nights for early mornings: think sunrise Pilates and sound baths. Unwind with barre classes and post-class matcha at MAJA Canggu, Bali, SHA Wellness Clinic, Spain or The Farm at San Benito in the Philippines. Cold feet? Stick them in a From saffron crème brûlée to mini gulab jamun cheesecake, Sage & Saffron by Aditi Dugar, Single Thread by Manu Chandra and Gaia Gourmet by Shilarna Vaze create vertitable edible art installations where Indian classics meet global favourites. Save paper (and your sanity)—digital invites are eco-friendly, elegant and will spare you the stress of awkward small talk when visiting relatives. Posh Invites by Gauri Agrawal and The Murphy Studio take away your logistical troubles by designing personalised wedding invitations. Roses and hydrangeas for a touch of romance; marigolds and jasmine for a traditional aesthetic; tulips and ranunculus for minimalists—trust Weddings by Gurleen M Puri and Interflora India to design your dream wedding space. Deep-cleansing facials to signature shaves, self-care for men has levelled up. Grooms can turn to Truefitt & Hill for luxury barbering or indulge in treatments like a Korean hair spa and face gym at Florian Hurel Hair Couture & Spa. No bridal trousseau is truly complete without at least one heritage weave. A Banarasi silk or a rich Kanjeevaram, passed down through generations, carries stories woven into every thread. Invest in an heirloom from Advaya, Tilfi or Ekaya. The infrared sauna penetrates deep into the skin to flush out toxins, soothe muscles and promote blood circulation. Sign up for a quick session at The Wellness Co. in Delhi, Salt World in Bengaluru or Reaviva Holistic Health in Mumbai. The technical artistry involved in the making of a piece of jadau jewellery—uncut diamonds, precious stones and pearls set in gold—gives it the stature of art. Tyaani, Jaipur Gems and The House of MBJ have you covered. The humble kolhapuris were the subject of much debate recently after they walked onto the Prada runway, but there’s no question about their comfort value. Designers like Aprajita Toor, The Sole Sisters and Sandalwali reimagine them for the wedding wardrobe: think zari, mirrorwork and pearl embellishments. A few days before the big day, sign up for this miracle treatment that can sculpt the face and reduce water retention at the Quan Spa, JW Marriott Mumbai, Kaya Kalp Spa, ITC Maurya New Delhi or Jiva Spa, Taj West End Bengaluru. From high-octane sangeet nights to a sundowner mehendi, mirrorwork is the playful alternative to an otherwise zardozi-heavy wedding wardrobe. Find your piece at Arpita Mehta, Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla or JJ Valaya. Add a pop-up manicure station to your mehendi festivities to queue up for some fun. Nail Rituals in Delhi, Studio Nails by Anisha Mulchandani in Mumbai and Nailbox in Bengaluru bring glamour and polish straight to your venue. In the intricate art of fragrance layering, oud is that versatile element that pairs well with vanilla, sandalwood and more. Luxury fragrance houses like Maison Francis Kurkdjian and Ajmal Perfumes are known for their refined takes on oud—elegant, addictive and as timeless as your vows. Does an intimate pre-ceremony to exchange vows and inside jokes without a crowd watching sound nice? Take a good photographer along—the folks at House On The Clouds, Joseph Radhik or The Wedding Filmer—to capture the moment. Rose quartz’s association with healing, love and emotional clarity makes it a befitting beauty companion to keep close in the lead-up to your wedding—especially for a glow that goes beyond skin-deep. RAS Luxury Oils and Dromen & Co offer beautifully crafted rose quartz facial tools. Pastels and neutral hues may often take centre stage, but rani pink’s unmistakable vibrance guarantees it a spot in a bride’s trousseau, like that fun cousin in your bridesquad. Find your bold fashion moment for the sangeet at Frontier Raas or House of Masaba. Kokum-urrak spritzers for a summer soirées, toddy-based nightcaps for winter sangeets: Master mixologists like Yangdup Lama and Pankaj Balachandran can keep things lush with potions highlighting Indian brands and local ingredients. Sculptural centrepieces, softly glowing taper candles, place settings in elegant calligraphy: The tablescape is emerging as the canvas to tell a visual story of togetherness. Designers like Altair by Janki Desai and Eeshaan Kashyap specialise in crafting immersive experiences—styling food, cocktails, tableware and decor to create cohesive and memorable sit-down dinners. If you’re looking to recreate that timeless Mughal charm through your bridal jewellery, look no further than uncut diamonds—or polki. Jaipur-based Raniwala 1881, Hazoorilal Legacy and Indriya by Aditya Birla can help you find the right pieces that carry the perfect balance of craftsmanship and modern elegance. There’s something about the Indianised bridal veil—lightweight tulle with intricate embroidery—that elevates your whole bridal look like little else. Designers like Sabyasachi, Gaurav Gupta and Falguni Shane Peacock know how to balance tradition with wearability. Whether it’s a quiet affair or a 700-person spectacle on your vision board, pulling it off needs a seasoned planner—like Devika Narain (known for detail-rich weddings) or Motwane Entertainment & Weddings (who can whip up larger-than-life productions). For that secret element that can take your wedding to a whole other level, craft a signature scent together—one that captures your story and lives on in memory. Brands like Jo Malone and Maison 21G offer bespoke fragrance experiences where you can co-create a scent to wear, gift or even diffuse throughout your celebration. After all the madness of wedding planning, unwind and recharge with a short yoga retreat at Dharana at Shillim or Ananda in the Himalayas—nothing like a weekend of vinyasa flows, gut-cleansing meals and natural quietude to reenergise you before the big show. Astrology likely played a role early in your relationship to help you spot red flags—so why leave the zodiac factor out of your big day? From Fizzy Goblet’s zodiac sandal heels and Mrinalini Chandra’s customised kaliras to Outhouse Jewellery’s celestial-inspired pieces, the stars truly align in the last alphabet of this wedding directory.

article_title: Janhvi Kapoor’s dream wedding reflects a new era of intimate celebrity unions
sub_title: Across India and beyond, celebrities are stepping away from grand productions for ceremonies that feel private, personal and true to them
article_content: When Janhvi Kapoor talks about her dream wedding, concepts like drone shots, elephant processions and endless pre-functions aren’t in the frame. In her It’s not about capability—Kapoor could command a stadium if she chose—but about intent. What she desires is an intimate ritual, not a production. “I know I want to get married in Tirupati. I definitely don’t want too many people there. I want it to be quick and I want the honeymoon to be very long,” she tells us. And she’s not alone. Across industries and time zones, stars are turning away from maximalist “all eyes on me” weddings in favour of something private, spiritual and stripped back. Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth tied the knot this year in a 400-year-old Telangana temple, announcing it with a single set of photographs. Alia Bhatt and Ranbir Kapoor married at The mood extends beyond India. Charli XCX married musician George Daniel at Hackney Town Hall in London with 20 close guests, in a Vivienne Westwood The draw of the big fat celebrity wedding hasn’t disappeared. But in an age of constant exposure—when even an airport look gets dissected–the wedding is the one moment stars want wholly for themselves. Kapoor’s generation in particular sees resonance in what feels genuine, not staged. That shift shows up in clothes, too. Kapoor imagines herself in a Manish Malhotra creation but wants something familiar and comfortable. Alia Bhatt wore an This doesn’t mean extravagance is dead. But the definition of “dreamy” has widened. For Janhvi Kapoor, it’s vows at Tirupati and the freedom of comfort. For others, it’s a balcony, a farmhouse or a restaurant. What’s appealing now is not scale but sincerity. So in the absence of any need to prove anything to the world, what’s left is the privilege of being present with oneself, your partner and those who truly matter. Isn’t that what marriage is about, anyway?

article_title: Two fine jewellery ateliers that are reimagining Indian heritage
sub_title: From rare gemstones and distinctive design to a hundred years of legacy craftsmanship, Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels and Mehta & Sons create bespoke creations that tell stories across generations
article_content: Jewellery is a reflection of the wearer. The necklace you pick to wear on a special day to the simple studs that adorn your ears on the daily—every trinket you choose tells your story. Two distinguished jewellery brands, Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels and Mehta & Sons, celebrate this individuality with their pieces—the unique cuts, gemstones and designs ensuring that there is something for every discerning customer. Scroll further to know more about the two brands, their design sensibilities, their founders and more. Since its inception in 2005, Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels has become synonymous with intricate craftsmanship, rare gemstones, and distinctive design. From heirloom classics to contemporary statements, each jewel is brought to life using a curated palette of the world’s finest treasures—Golconda diamonds, Colombian emeralds, Burmese rubies, Basra pearls, Kashmir sapphires, Paraiba tourmalines, and Baltic amber, set in 18K and 22K gold, often finished with unique polishes and textures. The founder, Dr. Anjali Bhimrajka’s journey into fine jewellery was shaped by artistic instinct and passion. With academic accolades including a Ph.D. in Alternative Medicine, Dr. Bhimrajka is a true polymath. She turned her childhood fascination into a lifelong calling, taking herself to the Gemological Institute of America, where she trained in jewellery design and diamond grading—formally setting the foundation for her namesake label. Every jewel at Anjali Bhimrajka Fine Jewels begins with ethically sourced diamonds and gemstones—selected not only for their brilliance, but for their integrity. Age-old techniques are not just preserved—they are reinterpreted through a modern lens, creating designs that feel timeless yet distinctly contemporary. Their latest collection, Rêve Parisien is an ode to the romance of Paris. It translates the charm of a bygone era into radiant elegance and modern sophistication.The collection introduces neckpieces, ear pendants, and rings with vibrant coloured and uncut diamonds, enhanced by blue sapphires and tanzanites—highlighted by mandarin garnets and colourful sapphires. For a hundred years, Mehta & Sons has been more than a jeweller—it has been a custodian of tradition, artistry, and trust. An ancestral house built on values passed down through generations, the brand remains deeply rooted, humble, and true to its heritage, even as it evolves to meet the aspirations of the modern world. Mehta & Sons began its journey almost a hundred years ago, in 1931, and to this day, every piece at the atelier brings with it this legacy of craftsmanship and quality. Carrying forward his ancestral heritage, Mr. Narendra Mehta has shaped Mehta & Sons into one of India’s most trusted names in fine jewellery. A man of vision and quiet strength, he believes that every creation must reflect not only artistry but also soul. For him, a jewel is more than design—it is emotion, value, and legacy, to be cherished by generations. His philosophy ensures that every piece leaving the atelier carries with it the same integrity and devotion that has defined the brand for a century. The artisans of Mehta & Sons honour tradition while embracing innovation. Known for their intricate gold-work, mastery in diamond settings, and the rare art of blending vibrant gemstones with precision, the house has perfected its craft over a century. Each jewel reflects the devotion of both artisan and founder—where craftsmanship is not just skill, but an inheritance. To mark its centenary, Mehta & Sons unveil their latest collections, Strata and Eterna—paying homage to their legacy while embracing modern luxury. The bridal line captures the grandeur and sentiment of Indian tradition, crafted as heirlooms of love. The collections feature diamond creations elevated with rare gemstones, exuding bold elegance and timeless charm. Both these brands are a celebration of heritage—tested by time, yet created for today. They aim to bridge the legacy of Indian heritage with a global sensibility, crafting modern heirlooms that transcend trends and generations.

article_title: 9 bridal makeup products that belong in every wedding day kit
sub_title: Call it your bridal toolkit for everything from toasts to tears
article_content: Some brides wouldn't dream of their ideal beauty look without enlisting the help of a We have curated a ready reckoner with the key makeup products in any kit along with tips on how to use them, so that you're well prepared for your big day. When you get down to brass tacks, Without proper prep, your skin can be something of a blotched nightmare. After all, you’ll want your makeup to hold up through the last selfie, toast and twirl. This makes primer extremely essential. The thumb rule is to use a You probably won’t get enough shut-eye during your wedding festivities, but this is the one time when you want to look your fresh-faced best. This requires a seriously heavy-duty A Lock in your base with a pressed or loose setting powder. One swipe of a brush will absorb excess oils to give a visibly flawless finish. A compact size will also be handy for touch-ups later. Your wedding day is the perfect opportunity to pack some punch with your eye makeup. Look for a palette that combines neutrals and metallic shades. Warm, earthy tones work best with Indian skin. Shades of gold, bronze and copper also do well together, and the modern Indian bride can opt for these colours without a second thought. A waterproof formula is the only answer to smudge-proof, sweat-proof and even tear-proof your eye makeup. Make sure to add a highly pigmented long-wear eyeliner to your makeup kit. Another non-negotiable? A mascara. But before you buy one, decide whether you’re looking for length or volume. A highlighter can serve as the perfect pick-me-up for your complexion, and provide a lit-from-within glow when applied to the high points of the face (cheekbones, tip of the nose, brow bones, and Cupid’s bow). Choose your formula according to the look you want to achieve—a powder highlighter will give you a matte look, a cream or balm version will leave you with dewy face, while a liquid highlighter will provide the most intense colour pay-off. The last step to your bridal makeup, lipstick is a staple. Keep a red, pink and a nude at the ready. While matte formulas will last the longest, don’t have any qualms about opting for a creamy option.

article_content: There’s something special about tying the knot at a place that is replete with history and tradition. For this couple, it was Naples—a favourite from one of their weekend getaways in Florida encouraged by her parents ‘Sunday Fundays’ tradition. It was only fitting then, that Jasmin Parikh and Hiren Babaria, chose to have their wedding at the newly renovated  Ritz-Carlton Naples in Florida. The venue’s quiet sophistication was the ideal backdrop, featuring swaying palms and turquoise waters, an amalgamation of tranquility and celebration. Quiet, joyful and endearing, Jasmin and Hiren's love story was the kind that revelled in a slower pace, unfolding gently over multiple dates. It started off with a message sent by Jasmin with the help of her aunt, and a reply from Hiren days later while he was on a trip to Hawaii. And then the conversations began, and translated to dates. Their first date in Dallas was cinematic, thoughtful and the connection was natural and instant. They had sushi at Uchi, spent time taking long walks in the rain, and cute gestures like holding an umbrella over her head had Jasmin convinced this could lead to more. Jasmin is from New Jersey and Florida, and Hiren is from Dallas. Their long-distance relationship certainly drove up airline ticket sales with the couple taking over 30 trips between cities like New York, Chicago, Orlando and Dallas. The proposal on a secluded beach in Oahu was much like their relationship, quiet and a celebration of their love. Jasmin had an inkling and got her nails done and got them matching outfits, a girl can never be too prepared. As they walked onto the beach during sunset hour, feeling the sand on their toes, Jasmin saw the flowers and the “Will You Marry Me” sign. Jasmin describes the feeling as surreal and although Hiren was fairly certain about the answer, he wanted to make a meaningful yet grand gesture. The celebrations began with an intimate welcome dinner at The Ritz-Carlton Naples. The property, which was recently renovated, provided the perfect backdrop with everything looking brand new. The couple’s interests found translation in the decor, food and the personalised details. The menu, curated by chef Satish, had a mix of traditional Gujarati dishes and international staples like sushi, incorporating all the flavours the couple loved. The following morning, the couple had the traditional Grah Shanti, a ritual to mark an auspicious beginning of the celebrations. This was followed by the Haldi ceremony where the couple was showered with turmeric and petals, with laughter and joy filling the air. The couple then took a dip in the ocean with their friends and family cheering them on. This sentiment was captured beautifully by P.Taufiq Photography. Sangeet night saw enthusiastic performances by friends and family, and a dance floor that was buzzing into the early morning with Foram Shah at the console. It ended with garba, a nod to their roots. The wedding ceremony had the couple promising each other a lifetime of love and happiness under a lush floral mandap, and in the background, the sound of waves and swaying palms. With that,  Ritz-Carlton Naples hosted a big Indian wedding, planned by Bharati Shah, Electric Karma International and supported ably by the floral decor work of Utopian events. The band, a favourite with the guests and the couple alike, and at the console was Empire Entertainment. Serenading the guests with melodies on her violin was Amy Serrano. A nod to her roots, the bride wore Tarun Tahiliani for the sangeet, wedding, and reception. She wore a custom Mani Jassal outfit for welcome night, and a custom-designed Haldi outfit by the bride’s sister. The groom wore Siddesh Chauhan for the welcome night. He wore a Tarun Tahiliani outfit for the sangeet, and his sherwani for the wedding was by Shyamal & Bhumika. He wore a soft pista green gently complementing the bride’s pink bridal lehenga. For the reception, he wore a deep maroon tuxedo to contrast with the bride’s ivory outfit. All of this was captured beautifully by PTaufiq Photography. Brought together by chance, this love story was etched in the memory of everyone who attended, and certainly made a case for finding love in the unlikeliest of places.

article_title: Expressions of joy
sub_title: Izzhaar, a gifting solutions brand is turning emotions into mementos for you and your loved ones
article_content: Finding the right gift that conveys the love, regard and care you have for someone can be a herculean task. Be it an anniversary, a wedding, or a festival—special moments like these deserve to be commemorated with thoughtful gifts. Taking the onus of giving your emotions a tangible form is Izzhaar, a brand born in 2014, that promises to make gifting emotional and intentional. Founded by Ruchita Bansal, a designer with a deep love for thoughtful aesthetics, Izzhaar began with one goal: to craft gifts and invitations that speak the language of the heart. Bansal’s brainchild wasn’t born because the world needed another gifting brand—it was because the founder thought that something was amiss. Izzhaar wanted to capture that feeling when a gift lights up someone's eyes, not because of how much it was worth, but because of its meaning. What started as a passion project soon evolved into a thriving business—one where every design is a reflection of affection, culture, and connection. Offering value for money gifting solutions, Izzhaar is known for its bespoke wedding hampers, artisanal invitations, home décor, and festive hampers. The brand offers exclusive options to their customers—be it a pastel-toned invitation inspired by a couple’s journey, or a sustainable hamper to reward hard-working employees; no two pieces are ever the same, because no two stories are the same. At the heart of it all is Bansal’s creative vision—guided by soul, not trend. “Luxury gifting isn’t about grandeur. It’s about care, connection, and meaning. We don't create to impress, we create to express,” she says. Izzhaar collaborates with artisans who believe in slow, impactful creation and are meticulous about the small details. The brand cares deeply about the planet, creating consciously with sustainable materials and focusing on pieces that become lasting keepsakes, not disposable gestures. With sustainability at its core and curated creativity in every detail, Izzhaar continues to create an impact in the modern Indian gifting scene.

article_title: This bride's classic red vision came alive with a Sabyasachi lehenga for her California wedding
sub_title: Dr Jasmine Singh's lehenga was hand-stitched and embroidered with traditional gold and silver threads, while the borders of her two veils featured handmade kiran fringing in hand-beaten gold and copper
article_content: For many brides, their wedding day is a unique opportunity to honour their heritage, often through fashion. Such was the case for Indian-American bride Dr Jasmine Singh, a psychiatrist based in California. “Even as a child, I knew – without a doubt – that no matter who I married, or when I married, I would have a Sikh wedding ceremony, and I would wear a traditional red Indian lehenga with gold embroidery,” she explains. “My mother has countless photos of me as a little girl dressed in a tiny red lehenga, adorned with a gold mathapatti and haathphool, and proudly wearing a bold red lip.” When the time came for Jasmine to curate her own wedding day looks for her marriage to Dr Sandeep Mann, she knew immediately that she wanted to work with Indian designers, especially on a red lehenga – that instantly recognisable Indian bridal outfit. “It mattered to me that my wedding outfit was made by hands and minds that understood the symbolism embedded in every motif and stitch,” she explains. “I wanted to wear something that wasn’t just beautiful, but meaningful; something that connected me to my culture and heritage.” Having become familiar with his work decades earlier, Jasmine immediately thought of turning to the celebrated Indian designer Sabyasachi (who memorably dressed Priyanka Chopra for her wedding celebrations) for her lehenga and jewellery. “I first heard about him when I was a student at UC San Diego,” she explains. “I remember being captivated by the news that an Indian designer had shown at Milan Fashion Week. Since then I’ve followed his career, watching him dress countless brides – including many of India’s most celebrated actresses.” Jasmine started by selecting her wedding day jewellery from Sabyasachi, while she went back and forth on which of his red lehenga to wear and how to customise it to suit her bridal vision – often having two-hour long video calls with his team in India. “The first piece I selected was the necklace, followed by the earrings and then the bangles – my mother insisted I include Sabyasachi polki bangles,” she says. “Then came the custom mathapatti, nath, and haathphool. Somewhere in between, I found myself gravitating towards a floral motif lehenga from the Red Collection in the Heritage series. I waited before making a final decision, wanting to be certain. Shortly after meeting Sabyasachi in person during a visit to Los Angeles, I knew it was the one.” The mathapatti was inspired by one of Sabyasachi’s first famous brides, the actress Anushka Sharma – though she wanted hers to feature South Sea pearls, to match the rest of her look. “I was told by the Sabyasachi jewellery director that any changes such as this would have to be approved by Sabyasachi Mukherjee himself,” she explains. “I was delighted when I learned that he had signed off on the changes. The piece was also custom made to the measurements of my head, which I thought was a great attention to detail, as it was custom-fitted to frame my face perfectly from ear to ear.” Indeed, Sabyasachi as a rule does not allow customisation, so it was up to Jasmine to convince him of her vision for the lehenga too. “After explaining my reasoning, some customisation was allowed,” she shares. “I discussed with him that I wanted my second veil for my head to be different from the first that would be wrapped around my body, so that it could add more visual interest, which they agreed to.” One particularly special touch was the floral motif on the skirt – a brand new design. “It resonated with me on a personal level – my name is Jasmine, after all – and it beautifully complemented the wedding’s setting,” she explains. “Alongside my production team, we built a custom structure on my family’s estate, nestled within the estate’s gardens, and centred our design concept around an enchanted garden of wildflowers. This lehenga echoed that vision perfectly, and wearing it felt like stepping into a dream I had helped create.” The Sabyasachi team also crafted a custom silk organza palla for the ceremony, finished with gold sequins and a tilla thread border. “In Sikh tradition, the groom wears the palla, which is handed to the bride by her father – symbolising the start of the couple’s spiritual journey,” explains Jasmine. “Sabyasachi graciously completed this bespoke piece in record time, and it arrived just days before the wedding. I was later told it had only been made once before – for the actress Katrina Kaif – making it all the more meaningful.” Unsurprisingly, a lot of craftwork went into Jasmine’s lehenga, which was hand-stitched and embroidered with traditional gold and silver threads, while the borders of her two veils featured handmade kiran fringing in hand-beaten gold and copper. “My lehenga arrived in California a few weeks before the wedding,” recalls Jasmine. “The first time I wore it was late at night, with my mother by my side. I slipped it on – it fit like a glove – and when I saw myself in the full-length mirror, I cried. I was on the phone with Sabena, the head of Sabyasachi, and she was deeply moved by my reaction. In that moment, it truly felt like my vision and dream had come to life.” With so much love and detail going into the look, it’s unsurprising that Jasmine intends to wear the pieces again. “I believe fashion should be both enjoyed in the present and preserved for future generations,” she says. “And I don’t think preservation should come at the cost of fully experiencing the joy of wearing something now.” For her, the entire process was a pinch-me moment. “I see myself as someone who embodies two cultures: born and raised in the United States, yet deeply in touch with my Indian heritage,” she says. “That duality, what I call biculturalism, can sometimes bring difficulties with identity and with managing the two opposing cultures, but sometimes the juxtaposition can be beautiful, and that is something I find in Sabyasachi’s designs: a rare and beautiful balance.”

article_title: Is your boyfriend planning a beach proposal? He needs to read this
sub_title: Learn everything to know about planning a perfect beach proposal, from tips on selecting a location to how to make a rain plan
article_content: A beach proposal is a favourite for a reason. The calm crashing of the waves, the feeling of your toes in the sand and the spectacular backdrop of the ocean sky at sunrise or sunset are a dreamy combination to craft the perfect romantic moment. Indians, especially, love beach proposals because they have all the makings of a Ahead, see all the proposal planning tips you’ll need to kick off your beach engagement. Choosing the right beach location is key to guaranteeing a beautiful proposal setting. First, consider the destination that feels right for the engagement. Is there a beach you often frequent together? It could be special to revisit this place in your romantic history for your proposal. Planning a beach vacation? Scout out the best beaches for proposals near your destination with a beautiful lookout, or seek a more private cove. If you are less familiar with the area, you might want to check online for frequented spots or ask your hotel concierge for any tips. If you’re staying at a resort, they may even have a special area on the property that can be the perfect location for your big moment. As you likely don’t want hundreds of spectators around that can take up prime sand real estate, it’s important to decide on a not-so-busy time to get down on one knee. Consider hitting the beach in the off-season when there aren’t as many sunbathers about or at an hour when the location is relatively empty, like when most people are at dinner. You can even plan a romantic picnic on the beach during this hour before you pop the question. It’s also important to consider the best ambience based on the time of day: not when the sun is too bright, but definitely when it’s just at the horizon. Not only will it be beautiful to watch (and give you an excuse to get your S.O. out there for the surprise), but the light will be wonderful for photos. Helpful hint: Bring a sweater or extra blanket in case the temperatures drop when the sun is no longer in sight. As I am well aware, bad weather can easily throw a wrench in your proposal plans. In my case, a windy forecast made my plans for a post-engagement dinner on the beach a less-than-ideal situation. So, we had to change the location for the second act of the proposal just hours prior. No matter your situation, it’s always important to have a rain contingency plan. Especially if you have hired a photographer or pre-planned a celebration afterwards, you may need to find another covered spot to pop the question. Always have a backup in place when you are first scouting out your ideal beach locale. Deciding on the right outfit for your proposal is a tricky task. On the one hand, you don’t want to give away the surprise by showing up overdressed for a beach day. But, you also probably want to look more polished than usual, especially if you’re documenting the proposal. Try to find a happy medium or create an excuse for a slightly Another important factor of your ensemble is that it needs a spot to hide a ring box. A jacket with an inner pocket, spacious pant pockets, or a bag can be key to keeping your surprise hidden away. Just be sure your hiding place is secure so you don’t leave the ring on the beach. While you will always have the memory of your proposal, it’s also fun to have images or videos of the special moment to come back to and share with your loved ones. One of the best solutions is to find a local photographer to document the moment as it happens. This can lead to a great photoshoot with you, your new fiancé and that engagement ring you spent months picking out. If you don’t want to hire a pro, you could also task a friend or family member to do the job with an iPhone. Just be sure they can stay hidden so as to not give away the surprise and are a trusted hand with tech. Once your partner (hopefully) says yes, it’s time for you both to celebrate. Don’t just plan the proposal itself. It’s a great idea to also have plans in place to take in the moment, whether in an intimate atmosphere or with your closest circle. A bottle of bubbly and a beach picnic can be the perfect way to enjoy your newly engaged bliss. Or, you can make a reservation at a nearby restaurant for a more polished toast. Some to-be-weds like to kick off their engagement era with a bang and invite friends and family for a surprise engagement party. Just be sure you’ve had previous talks of engagement and know it’s a done deal before you have anyone fly out for the festivities.

article_title: A Czech bride, a Telugu groom and an Indian baraat in Prague
sub_title: Two cultures, two venues and one unforgettable celebration. Here’s how event and wedding planning company, RVR Eventz & Design and RVR PRO meticulously crafted a wedding day for this couple, across continents and traditions
article_content: In a world saturated with left swipes, fleeting connections and catfishing stories, Karolina Ebel, a lawyer-turned-entrepreneur, and Chaitanya Aluru, an engineer, found the kind of love written about in fairytales. It was a rainy day in New York, and a thoughtful connection over a dating app that sparked this love story. Barely a month into the relationship, Karolina knew that this was the man she was meant to marry. There was no grand moment, no epiphany, just quiet certainty. At a cliffside near Carmel-by-the-Sea, California, Chaitanya surprised Karolina with a wedding proposal, two weeks before their formal engagement. Saying ‘yes’ at her favourite spot with Chaitanya’s handwritten note hidden inside a bouquet of roses was surreal. It was this note that Karolina kept close to her heart, embroidering it on her wedding veil with words that read: The couple commemorated their union with a three-day wedding in Prague, Czech Republic, complete with an Indian When it came to choosing a wedding destination, Prague held a special place for the couple. It was Karolina’s hometown, and a place they had visited together on a vacation early in their relationship. For them, the city’s old-world charm, connection to the bride’s roots, and stark contrast to their fast-paced Silicon Valley life made it the perfect location. Chaitanya, who holds his Indian heritage and family traditions close, envisioned incorporating a traditional Hindu wedding. The couple’s shared vision for their wedding was to honour both cultures, blending vibrant Indian rituals within a European setting. To bring this vision to life, they chose the experienced team at RVR Eventz & Design. The couple hosted two ceremonies across iconic venues in Prague—an Indian wedding at the Mandarin Oriental and a civil ceremony and reception at the grand baroque Chateau Troja. The Indian wedding festivities began with an outdoor traditional The Czech civil ceremony, by contrast, was a formal legal celebration officiated by a registrar, followed by a reception with European flair, filled with food, drinks and dancing. One of the most unforgettable moments of the wedding was when the Locals and tourists paused to pull out their phones, capturing what felt like a movie scene unfolding in real life. Chaitanya, in a traditional sherwani, led the procession with friends and family dancing joyfully behind him. The air was filled with laughter, flower petals and the infectious rhythm of celebration. This wasn’t just a wedding tradition; it was a joyful moment of cultural fusion. Planning a wedding that spanned continents and cultures came with its fair share of challenges. Much of the wedding décor, bridal wear, and ceremonial items were shipped from India via air cargo. Several vendors and team members had to navigate visa approvals, and Prague’s rainy weather threw a curveball the day before the outdoor ceremony. “This was one of the toughest weddings I’ve planned,” says Priya Maganti, CEO at RVR Eventz & Design. “Planning a wedding in a new country is always a challenge, but every country I’ve worked in before had already seen Indian weddings, and they knew what to expect. Prague was different.” From explaining rituals to helping guests embrace cross-cultural customs, the team handled every detail with care. “The concept of an Indian wedding was new to many of the Czech vendors and guests, but now there is a growing appreciation and understanding of what it involves,” Maganti adds. Guests on both sides leaned in to celebrate each other’s cultures, whether it was through clothing, food, or participating in rituals. Czech guests wore lehengas and saris for the Hindu ceremony, while Indian guests donned elegant Western formals for the civil wedding. In a whirlwind of legal permits, hand-embroidered veils, tailor-made blazers, and a multi-cuisine menu, RVR Eventz & Design and RVR PRO ensured that every element of the couple’s vision came to life with authenticity and heart.

article_title: Sweet treats for the big moments
sub_title: The Laddoo Wala is making weddings special with sweets that are rooted in tradition and made with a modern hand
article_content: Weddings today are more than just ceremonies. They are expressions of identity, story, and emotion. The Laddoo Wala, an Indian mithai and savoury brand, honours this shift by reimagining the role of mithai in modern celebrations. The brand has set out to redefine the way Indian sweets are experienced—not as festive afterthoughts, but as elevated essentials. TLW focuses on clean ingredients, refined flavours, and thoughtful presentation. Their laddoos are hand-rolled in small batches with less to no sugar, using alternative sweeteners like jaggery and dates and with no added colours or preservatives. The result is a sweet that feels both nostalgic, healthy and refreshingly new. But TLW isn’t just about laddoos. Their growing repertoire includes silky barfi blocks, crisp savoury blends, and seasonal offerings that bring variety and versatility to any moment of celebration. Each product is developed with a strong attention to detail, balancing indulgence with today’s evolving preferences. With options that are gluten and cholesterol free, and naturally sweetened, there is something for everyone. The brand’s approach extends beyond taste. At TLW, design is an integral part of the experience. Their packaging is thoughtful, with embossed boxes that evoke warmth and nostalgia, and trays that become part of your home. Each wrap, label, and note is crafted with care, often carrying a little story inside—adding another layer of meaning to the gift. What truly sets TLW apart is the emotion embedded in every bite. Some connect with the richness of the motichoor, others with the gooey texture of their Every wedding the brand is a part of is approached as a creative collaboration. Whether it’s bridesmaid proposals, mehendi favours, or welcome hampers, they work closely with families and couples to co-create something truly exclusive. This year, they’ve expanded their repertoire with playful yet elegant additions like the ‘Laddoo Pops’ and ‘Savour Me’s’, a fresh take on the traditional laddoos and savouries that are perfect to share, to travel with, and for interactive displays. They carry craft and flavour with a touch of whimsy—designed for the contemporary celebration. Alongside this, the brand’s bespoke trays, savoury tins, and new barfi block formats bring depth and variety to your wedding table, all while staying rooted in Indian flavour profiles. At TLW, it’s the small things that make a wedding unforgettable, the welcome box that feels like a hug, the flavour that sparks a childhood memory, the handwritten message inside a hamper that makes someone pause. The brand believes in thoughtfulness and in creating mithai experiences that are as meaningful as the moment they belong to.

article_title: From Pichwai to Zardozi: Crafting a wedding of meaning and elegance
sub_title: What began as a chance encounter turned into a tale of culinary adventures, thoughtful gestures and shared calm—culminating in a deeply personal wedding at Raffles, Udaipur
article_content: They say matches are made in heaven, and perhaps that’s true, but matches are also made over shared plates of food. As they say, the way to one’s heart is through the stomach, after all. Sidharth Sharma, a restaurateur and owner of several renowned hospitality ventures across New York and New Jersey, knew this all too well. Sharma met Dhara Patel, a physician assistant, also from New Jersey, at a friend’s birthday in the Poconos, and it didn’t feel like they were meeting for the first time—there was a quiet familiarity, discussions about food they enjoyed, and shared experiences about growing up Indian-American. “For our first date, I took Dhara on a romantic picnic,” reminisced Sharma. After many personalised food tours and candle-lit conversations through the years and around the world, he popped the question in Napa Valley, surrounded by beautiful vineyards—recreating their first picnic date. “That first date stayed with me—the excitement, the ease, the joy of it all. When he recreated it in Napa to propose, it took me right back to that feeling. Saying yes wasn’t even a question—it was the easiest, happiest answer of my life,” Patel gushed. A dreamy wedding followed, rooted in the couple’s approach to love—grounded, enduring, and filled with genuine joy. The celebration of love took place across three days at Raffles Udaipur, a lakeside property known for its European-meets-Indian architecture and quiet luxury. The wedding was an homage to the couple’s cultural roots, and every detail was artfully preserved by P.Taufiq Photography—the team that captured both the grand entries and the quiet, in-between moments that depict a love story. The festivities opened with a spirited welcome lunch spread across Raffles Udaipur and Taj Lake Palace, where guests were greeted by the pulse of dhols, the melodies of Rajasthani folk musicians, and vibrant cultural performances—Kachchi Ghodi dancers, flutists, Raavan Hatta artists, and Matka performers. While welcoming their guests, the bride’s mehendi—crafted by Jayshree Panchal—became a conversation of its own, adorned with Pichwai cows, Ganeshji, peacocks, elephants, and swans, weaving together symbols of grace, good fortune, and devotion. This set the tone for a weekend of thoughtful detail and joyful celebration, both high on emotion and aesthetically unforgettable. The Mehendi and Sangeet took over the Great Park, transitioning from tropical Rajasthani day motifs—florals, birdcages, and pops of colour—to a twilight fantasy of chandeliers and lush floral canopies. The bride wore a custom Mayyur Girotra lehenga embroidered with a menagerie of birds and elephants for the Mehendi and a custom StudioSush floral blouse, later transforming into a shimmering gold StudioSush lehenga paired with a Rahul Mishra blouse for the Sangeet. “All of my looks were thoughtfully assembled by Style by Susmita. She brought my vision to life through carefully coordinated outfits, custom-designed jewelry, and beautiful hair and makeup,” said Patel. The groom matched her energy in color-coordinated daytime wear and a custom PourLui look for the Sangeet. The second day began with Haldi. Held at the poolside, it was a riot of laughter, turmeric, and sunlight. Mughal-inspired, vibrant floral decor was the backdrop as friends and family playfully applied haldi while showering the couple with rose petals and love. The Varmala ceremony followed. It unfolded beneath ‘The Promise Tree’—a towering floral sculpture symbolising growth and commitment. The wedding ceremony took place indoors, under a mirrored aisle and a floral mandap conceptualised as a ‘Mirror of Forever’. Lagnageet artists, led by Darshana Gandhi, lent a soulful backdrop to the pheras. Simultaneously, guests rang bells during the pheras, infusing the ritual with a collective sense of sentimentality. As the pheras concluded, guests gathered around the couple, walking them out in a moment of shared joy and intimacy, only to be surprised by a display of fireworks that lit up the night sky. For some prior key rituals, the bride chose to honor her legacy by wearing heirloom gold bangles from her grandmother and her mother’s handloom saree. However, for the ceremony, the bride wore a full custom deep-red Mayyur Girotra lehenga, intricately embroidered with zardozi, motifs of peacocks, elephants, and flowers—each representing strength, love, and prosperity. The groom complemented her in an ivory sherwani, also by Mayyur Girotra. The wedding dinner that evening channelled the charm of an Indo-English garden, complete with native foliage, warm brass accents, and moody romantic lighting, courtesy of AJEventsIndia. The atmosphere was made all the more memorable by singer Akanksha Bhandari, whose soulful performance left the guests spellbound. The final day began with a pastel-toned party by the pool, accompanied by vibrant live music from percussionist Monark Khatri. The decor was inspired by the floral movement and spinning windmills, complete with springtime abandon. Set against Raffles’ tranquil waters, it was equal parts chic and carefree. The bride wore a bell-accented pastel sharara set by Payal Singhal while the groom complemented her in a linen bomber kurta from the same designer. As the sun dipped, a cocktail hour was arranged at the main fountain—an evening made memorable by illusionist Dhruv Chauhan and violinist Erna Daugaviete. The last dance of the weekend was the reception, titled ‘Midnight Opulence’. Guests danced the night away on the celestial floor at the black-and-metallic themed function, set under black crystal chandeliers and a canopy of white florals as the couple looked radiant in sculptural metallic ensembles by Amit Aggarwal. “Our vision was brought to life by two planners—one from India and one from America—seamlessly blending the two cultures. A3Cube Events (India) managed the on-the-ground execution in Udaipur, overseeing vendor coordination, guest arrivals, setup, and more. Meanwhile, Events by Vaishali (USA) focused on the finer details of the program, ensuring each event flowed smoothly, from start to finish,” said the couple. Every element of the Sharma-Patel wedding reflected a deeply personal touch, like custom stationery by V1964, a wedding website designed by Patel, menu-inspired invitations paying homage to Sharma’s culinary world, totes adorned with a watercolor portrait of their dog, Circuit, and personalized shawls, hand-calligraphed live by Inpreet Kaur. “Each night, the dance floor came alive under DJ Gaurav Sood and DJ Deval Patel, who set the perfect vibe from the Mehendi to the reception for a diverse crowd of guests—including 250 from the States and 150 from India,” said Sharma. The week’s emotional highs and personal moments at the afterparty were soundtracked by DJ Mowgli (Samuel Cherian, the friend who first introduced them). For the couple, this wasn’t just a weekend of celebration—it was a manifestation of the values they hold dear, the love they cherish, and the life they’re building together.

article_title: Sparkling through generations: Jewellery that endures
sub_title: Here’s a look at Rare Heritage, a bridal couture and fine jewellery brand making strides in India’s luxury jewellery landscape
article_content: Bridal couture plays a pivotal role in the grandeur of an Indian wedding, where fashion is as much a spectacle as the ceremonies themselves. Bridal outfits are representative of tradition, status, and personal taste, with designers translating cultural heritage into couture statements. Rare Heritage, a brand under the Mehta Emporium umbrella, was founded to add value to the country’s bespoke bridal jewellery. Starting out as a specialized bridal couture hub in 2014, the brand has now transformed into a premier fine jewellery house. The expansive 5,000 sq. ft. Mumbai atelier is both a creative sanctuary and an experiential showroom, making it the go-to destination for India's brides. Built on compelling paradoxes—premium yet approachable, selective but inclusive, it offers something for everyone, from understated minimalists to bold statement-makers. Rare Heritage has been a part of high-profile celebrations in the country while being endorsed by celebrities like Sonam Kapoor and Kareena Kapoor Khan. Every design is driven by a narrative, transforming individual pieces into legacy treasures meant to be passed down through generations. The brand’s insights into today’s bride offers a glimpse into the ask—pieces that are contemporary and yet timeless. Rare Heritage crafts collections that maintain relevance across decades. Each piece embodies cultural heritage, blending ancestral techniques with fresh perspectives to create deeply personal connections that extend far beyond ornamental value. The brand’s three directors, Manushi Singh, Nakshatra and Varun Mehta lead with vision. Singh’s design philosophy revolves around creating enduring relevance—pieces that feel modern yet possess the power to outlive fleeting trends. Her sophisticated aesthetic sensibility and forward-thinking approach have established the brand's authoritative presence in India's luxury jewellery landscape. His design methodology focuses on generating that transformative moment—when a bride connects deeply with a piece, creating bonds that extend well beyond the wedding day. Mehta’s perspective seals the deal, as he ensures that every design is mindful of the legacy it carries. article_title: Twelve years, one weekend, and a lifetime of love

article_content: Some love stories unravel with such quiet inevitability, it's as if they were always meant to be. Bride Akesha Sanjay and groom Aakash Thakor grew up just minutes apart from each other in South Florida, yet, like every romantic meet-cute, their story only began the summer before senior year of high school. “Looking back, it’s funny to think how many times our paths must have crossed—sharing mutual friends, going to the same community events, probably even standing in the same rooms,” Akesha mentions. They met at a Miami Heat NBA Finals watch party; Akesha, as always, was locked in—cheering, yelling at the screen—when Aakash noticed her, amused but intrigued. Little did they know that this was just the beginning of their forever. They quickly became high-school sweethearts—what started as a teenage friendship turned into a lifelong bond, one that endured distance, time zones, and countless changing careers. “Despite the miles, we always found our way back to each other,” they share. Fast forward to 12 years later, Aakash proposed to Akesha at sunset in Cabo, and the rest, like they say, is history. “I had a feeling it was coming—after so many years together, you kind of just know. But nothing could’ve prepared me for how beautiful and thoughtful it was. He had reserved a private stretch of beach at a gorgeous resort and planned an intimate dinner just for the two of us. The sun was setting, the ocean was in front of us—it was a moment I’ll never forget,” Akesha exclaims. So, when it came to their wedding, they knew it had to be a celebration of their story—a blend of grand gestures surrounded by their closest family and friends and a little bit of ‘Florida’ in all the celebrations to honour the city where it all began. Set against the Waldorf Astoria Riviera Maya, the backdrop was perfect. “It allowed us to have our dream sunset wedding and offered a variety of venues for each event, making every celebration feel unique and closer to our Floridian roots,” adds the bride. PTaufiq Photography captured the nuances of every smile, sentiment, and hidden undertone in pictures preserved for life. And there was ample to be captured, for each event boasted a different theme. The couple teamed up with Mala Events to bring their dream wedding weekend to life, curating every detail with intention and heart. Once the venue was secured, their vision truly took shape. The celebrations kicked off with a joyful joint Haldi ceremony, setting the tone for a weekend full of colour and culture. The welcome party channelled their shared love for Mexican cuisine, Latin music, and laid-back Florida vibes. The Saatak ceremony was a seamless blend of Indian tradition and modern design exemplified by Akesha’s ombré pink Manish Malhotra lehenga, a piece that “combined classic craftsmanship with contemporary flair”, she adds. The couple exchanged vows at sunset, with the beach as their breathtaking backdrop. Akesha wore a stunning Sabyasachi lehenga paired with a delicate Christian veil, while Aakash complemented her look in a regal Tarun Tahiliani sherwani. “It was the perfect expression of who we are—rooted in tradition, but shaped by a modern worldview,” she shares. The Sangeet pulsed with the vibrant energy of Miami—think neon colours, palm trees, and dancing late into the night. That was followed by a sleek black-tie reception, combining elegance and modern flair with glowing candles, cascading chandeliers, and the bride’s bold Gaurav Gupta gown stealing the spotlight. A surprise performance by British singer-songwriter Jay Sean, blending American and Indian hits that had all the guests on their feet. While DJ Sharad of DJ USA curated an electrifying set that kept the energy high and the dance floor packed all night long. Prashe Decor transformed each venue into a reflection of the couple’s cultures and personalities—seamlessly blending vibrant florals with refined, elegant elements. Musaafer, helmed by Michelin-starred Chef Mayank Istwal and his team, curated an unforgettable culinary journey, masterfully balancing traditional flavours with modern flair. Choosing PTaufiq was effortless; Aakash and Akesha had long admired their work. Surrounded by their closest family and friends, the couple’s wedding was truly a heartwarming reminder of love transcending boundaries.

article_title: 17 unique engagement party ideas for every type of couple
sub_title: An engagement party is a fun way to start your celebrations on a high note and bring together friends and family who might join you along your wedding journey
article_content: Whether you’re planning a proposal or recently said ‘yes,’ you might be brainstorming engagement party ideas to kick off your Ahead, we round up unique engagement party ideas to help you get inspired for your own pre-nuptial fête. From cocktail parties to fun activities, see a few ways to make the most of your engagement season. No need to wait a few weeks or months to celebrate your engagement. If you’re planning a proposal (and are 100% sure your partner will accept), consider following up getting down on one knee with a surprise Rather than Who doesn’t love a good poolside bash? Guests can take a dip, soak up the sun and lounge by the water. A theme is always fun: opt for a tropical aesthetic, complete with crowd-pleasing margaritas and piña coladas. Keep things refreshing with boozy popsicles as a sweet treat, and don’t forget to have some baskets around stocked with sun essentials—think sunscreen, pool towels and sunglasses. The “I do” BBQ is a classic engagement party idea, and one that requires minimal party planning for the couple who prefers a laid-back yet tasteful affair. Ideal for the spring and summer seasons, it’s also easy to tailor to your surroundings, be it an indoor grill, communal rooftop or a full backyard setup. For cocktails, keep it simple with spiked lemonade pitchers and a well-stocked beer tub. Don’t forget the ice and the vegetarian options to balance out the burgers and hot dogs. Add a personal touch with a signature BBQ sauce, French fry bar or a make-your-own ice cream station. You can check out Pinterest for further inspiration. Halloween isn’t the only time of year you can dress up—and a costume party can also serve as the perfect front for a surprise engagement announcement if you’ve kept it under wraps. If going for full-on costumes isn’t your style, a subtle engagement party theme can be just as lively. Perhaps, a throwback to a Roaring Twenties speakeasy, complete with Champagne towers, a live jazz band and a list of Prohibition-inspired signature cocktails. If you feel like donning ’70s threads, a roller disco might be just the groovy ticket; or, for an air of mystery and opulence, a murder mystery masquerade. If you’re a pair of film buffs, host a movie night for your entourage. Transform your abode into a home cinema by renting a projector and popcorn machine. You could also make it a pyjama-themed party and encourage your guests to come in comfy PJs. Whether you opt for an indoor theatre or a snug, outdoor setup, the ambience is key. Enhance the cosy feel with plush blankets, a wide selection of beverages and, of course, movie theatre candy. Choose an all-time classic or romcom for the main feature, or showcase your own collection of cherished home videos and photos for that extra personal touch. It’s the perfect excuse to be cheesy, after all. A late-morning affair is a particularly chic idea for your engagement party, Whether in your own backyard or a local park, a picnic is a wholesome get-together for the low-maintenance couple. Craft a delectable cheese board, adorned with a selection of charcuterie, sandwiches and lemonade for beverages. Skip the live band; grab your speaker and set the mood with your specially curated Spotify playlist. To accommodate any dietary restrictions, encourage guests to contribute their favourite finger foods. You can even embrace a Parisian-themed picnic, with an array of fruits and jams, well-paired wines and madeleines. Or, transport your luncheon to the sun-kissed charm of Positano with a refreshing Caprese salad, Aperol spritzes and bougainvillaea centrepieces—and don’t forget the limoncello digestif. (However, A cocktail party proves that glamour need not strain your budget, favouring light bites over a full-course meal. Hire a mixologist to craft a signature cocktail inspired by the happy couple. The bartender could also offer a cocktail-making class, and guests can leave with a personal cocktail-making set as a party favour. Also, you can’t go wrong with a live band. For a close-knit group of friends, rent out a cabin or a couple of glamping tents for a weekend retreat. A grown-up take on summer camp, you can hike along scenic trails during the day, and when the sun sets, gather around the bonfire to swap nostalgic stories while roasting marshmallows and eating s’mores. For the newly engaged couple seeking an elevated experience, indulge in a wine-tasting escapade with picturesque views. (For beer drinkers, a brewery promises an equally enjoyable outing.) Depending on where you live, you can arrange for a tour bus or an organised winery trail for a day of vineyard hopping. And, should you prefer the comfort of your home, simply hire a sommelier for a private wine-tasting session. Just don’t forget the hors d’oeuvres and cheese. Hit the deck with your fiancé and your favourite crew for a boat engagement party. Planning this event is as easy as chartering a boat in a nearby marina for a fun celebration on the water. Be sure to make sure guests can enjoy sips and nibbles by bringing on catering or hiring an on-board staff to keep the cruise in high spirits. Whether you love an intimate concert or a night out dancing, hiring live musicians for your engagement party can absolutely step up your celebration. Take time to find the right artists that can set the tone of your event and have them fill your party venue with the perfect soundtrack for your festivities. Since a wedding is a joining of two families, why not get your two sides better acquainted by making your engagement party a family reunion? Bring everyone together, either at your own home or a fun destination, where you can make introductions and create closer bonds between your extended family members. Another perk of this style of event? Everyone will be a little friendlier by the time they hit the dance floor at your wedding or sit around the table at future holiday dinners. Want your guests to do more than just mix and mingle over food? Why not make your engagement party a special carnival night where they can play games, win prizes and enjoy nostalgic fair treats? To bring this idea to life, you could DIY game booths or even bring in large carnival rentals to transform an outdoor space into the perfect summer night celebration. Crashing waves, crackling fire and a sunset over the horizon are the perfect recipe for a great beachside engagement party. Either book a private event space at a beachside restaurant or get a permit to put together your own celebration that has a coastal flair. Get engaged in the winter? Take advantage of a snowy backdrop and host a cold-weather celebration inspired by an après-ski outing in the mountains. Hot cocktails, fondue and décor with cosy elements you would find at the base of the slopes can help bring this party theme to life.

article_title: A conversation between Bengal’s artistry and Gujarat’s heritage
sub_title: Naina Jain creates a balance of traditional craftsmanship and contemporary elegance with this collection of handcrafted Bandhani sarees
article_content: A lot of different elements take centre stage at Indian weddings—dramatic family members, buffets of delicious food, sangeet performances to popular Bollywood numbers, but, arguably, the bridal outfit steals the show. It’s more than just attire—it’s a canvas of tradition, identity, and artistry. As generations of women adorn themselves in six yards of heritage for their special day, Naina Jain’s collection for the Vogue Wedding Atelier brings together two of India’s rich textile traditions—Bandhani from Gujarat and embroidery from Bengal—in a range of saris designed for women who are both contemporary and in touch with their roots. Renowned for reviving and reimagining Indian textile traditions, Jain’s work celebrates Bandhani—a centuries-old tie-and-dye technique predominantly practiced in western India—with a modern sensibility. Each saree in the collection is meticulously handcrafted by skilled artisans, who tie thousands of minuscule knots into the fabric before dyeing it, resulting in intricate patterns steeped in culture. What truly sets this collection apart is its thoughtful amalgamation of Bandhani with Bengal’s celebrated embroidery techniques, executed by master embroiderers using zardozi, aari, and intricate French knot work. These embellishments exude a delicate opulence, weaving together the visual language of two culturally rich regions into a single, harmonious narrative. The Bengal-inspired embroidery infuses a soft grace into the bold, geometric and organic patterns of Bandhani, striking the perfect balance between structure and fluidity. Floral and animal motifs rendered in detailed embroidery lend an earthy charm to the vivid Bandhani base, transforming each sari into a unique piece of wearable art. The color palette—ranging from jewel-toned maroons and purples to soft pastels and earthy neutrals—further enhances this cross-cultural aesthetic, appealing to both traditional and modern sensibilities. Every sari is more than just a garment; it is an heirloom-in-the-making, symbolising countless hours of labour, intergenerational knowledge, and a deep reverence for India’s diverse textile traditions. Jain’s approach goes beyond fashion; her collection is a celebration of artisanship, sustainability, and regional collaboration. By interweaving Gujarat’s Bandhani, Varanasi’s luxurious weaves, and Bengal’s intricate embroidery, she pays homage not only to technique but also to the communities and stories behind each creation. Whether worn at weddings, festive occasions, or intimate gatherings, these saris resonate with women who cherish authenticity, artistry, and legacy. In an age of fleeting trends, Jain’s collection is a timeless ode to slow, mindful craftsmanship—honoring the past while embracing the elegance of the present.

article_title: How to propose like a pro: Nail these dos and avoid these don’ts
sub_title: Planning to pop the big question? From meaningful locations to post-proposal plans, here are our dos and don’ts for how to propose
article_content: Getting ready to pop the big question, but feeling a bit lost about how to propose? You may have the engagement ring, already tailored to your partner’s ring size and the possibilities for the perfect proposal story swirling in your head. Perhaps you have a few marriage proposal ideas already. A rose-petaled scavenger hunt through your Resist the urge to follow fleeting engagement fads; your wedding proposal deserves to be as one-of-a-kind as your First and foremost, have all the essential conversations about your future with your partner. You want to make sure that marriage is something they are not only open to, but are determined to do. If family is important to your significant other, consider talking to their loved ones to ask permission before getting down on one knee. Surprise proposals are becoming less common, with couples often spending several years together before marriage. According to Put simply, your partner shouldn’t be caught completely off guard by your proposal timing, but the execution is open to personal touches and surprises. In our era of Plan what you want to say beyond the standard, “Will you marry me?” However, it’s best to plan out in bullet points rather than a typed up monologue. You don’t want to sound too robotic or be profusely sweating because you Location matters as well. Choose a spot that holds sentimental value, like you had your first date or where you met during freshman orientation week seven years ago. Speaking of location, it's best to opt for a low-key proposal. Some may love the public display, but emotions can run high and, in general, nobody wants to be proposed to amidst a crowd of tourists, traffic or Mumbai construction—especially if your love is on the timid side. No flash mobs. No busy restaurants. And, absolutely no jumbotrons. (Unless that’s something your partner will love and you’re 100% sure they’ll say yes.) Considering whether to get a photographer document your proposal? Think ahead to ten years from now, when you’ll want to revisit the moment. Or, perhaps the next day when you want to make an engagement announcement on social media. It’s never a bad idea think about hiring a proposal photographer or videographer, or ask a trusted best friend to document the big moment. If this feels impossible to do without spoiling the intimacy, incorporate mementos (like the letter) into the romantic proposal that you can keep or take pictures of afterward. It doesn’t have to be a full-blown photo shoot either. Just capturing the moment can be something that you and the love of your life can cherish forever. Getting down on one knee to propose is a tradition passed down from the medieval era, when knights would do so as a sign of chivalry. Today, the practice continues as a gesture of devotion and reverence to your partner when asking for their hand in marriage. Of course, getting down on one knee is absolutely optional. Just be sure to know for sure if you want to follow the tradition before your proposal takes place. Choose to do it at the last minute and might end up wavering in an awkward semi-lunge. Even if you only practise one time, saying the words you’re planning for your proposal will help you prepare and calm some of those nerves. Rehearse in front of a mirror, to a close friend, or to your pet. You’ll be able to sense how your script flows and what feels most natural to you. Also, remember to practise your physicality—like kneeling or grabbing their left hand to put on the ring. Of course, it doesn’t have to be perfect. Flubbing some words when getting emotional during the real thing will likely be endearing to your partner, rather than a reason for them to say no. If you want to keep an element of surprise for your proposal, it’s best to keep the engagement ring well hidden. That said, you don’t want to lose it either. A loose ring falling through a hole in your pocket onto a sandy beach is the worst-case scenario. Instead, find a secure place where you can stow the ring—preferably in its box—and make sure it’s well concealed. Remember that this is for you, too. Don’t let the stress overwhelm the joy of the occasion—remember, some nerves are good! As the proposer, you have the power to plan something that makes both of you happy. If you’re contemplating a more elaborate or destination proposal, consider hiring a proposal planner to assist with the grandeur of the event. While definitely a splurge, it’s an investment in your well-being if you’re not much of a planner and potentially the rest of your lives. After popping the question, have something special set up to celebrate afterward. You can pop a bottle of champagne, make a reservation at their favourite restaurant, or even set up a small engagement party with friends and family. You’ll absolutely want to savour in the rush after they say ‘yes’ and continue to enjoy in that moment. When your engagement day arrives, the most important thing on your task list to remember is the ring. article_content: Just like any storyteller’s classic true love trope, it was the red string of fate (a theory that connects two individuals who are destined to meet by an invisible red thread) that poetically brought Shlok Garg and Revathi Gudi together. They were the epitome of high school sweethearts. Always in the same space and within each other’s peripheral vision—stealing glances and making do with momentary nods in the high-tension passageways of school. What started as two teens making time for each other between cheerleading and basketball practices, all while planning dates in their hometown of Edison, New Jersey, transformed into something worthwhile in the most unpredictable way. But when life pulled them apart after graduation, love faced its greatest test. Through heartbreak, distance, and life’s many twists, Shlok and Revathi’s connection endured, waiting for the perfect moment to crescendo. They always knew their love story was special—fast forward a few more years, their journey came full circle with a dreamy proposal on a glittering rooftop in New York City, with Manhattan’s skyline unfurling around them and their beloved pet, Mochi, at their feet. With the vision of Aria Events weaving every detail and Luxx Escapes curating an impeccable guest experience, Shlok and Revathi's dream destination wedding unfolded like a vibrant tapestry blending South Indian rituals, Punjabi exuberance, and Spanish flair. One breathtaking island, two hundred enthusiastic guests, and a weekend-long reverie were all that was needed to make the celebration perfect. Mochi, of course, made it across the Atlantic Ocean from New Jersey to Spain for the big day, fully embracing each event in coordinating custom outfits made to match the couple. The celebrations kicked off with a vibrant henna ceremony, bathed in rich hues of green. The warm, intimate evening was filled with rhythmic beats of dholki and live folk tunes that made the night crackle with anticipation. The following day welcomed a rustic, Spanish-inspired welcome lunch that set the stage for the wedding weekend and transported guests straight into the heart of Iberian culture. With sun-drenched terraces, vibrant blooms, and culinary delights that paid homage to the island’s heritage, it was a sensorial feast that set the perfect tone for the celebrations to come. Later that evening, the Sangeet unfolded in a whirl of glamour. The venue transformed into a glittering dreamscape of mirrors, crystals, and soaring florals. Spanish flamenco dancers and guitarists from Azúcar intertwined their artistry with high-energy LED performances, while Kunal Lamba curated a dazzling entertainment experience. Platinum Roadshow’s DJ Raj Minocha, kept the dance floor alive into the early hours, weaving a soundscape as electric as the night itself. The second day of festivities began with a haldi ceremony—a fun-filled affair that saw a beautiful setup of vibrant marigold blooms set against the golden hour and the serene waterfront, with every joy-drenched moment documented exquisitely by P.Taufiq Photography. As the wedding day unfolded, the Atlantic Ocean bore witness to a scene straight out of a dream—soft pastel florals framing the sun-kissed altar, violinists serenading the sea breeze with classic Indian melodies, and the horizon igniting as fireworks crowned Shlok and Revathi's vows. At that moment, their love was infinite. For the reception, the couple turned the clock back to the roaring twenties. A Great Gatsby-themed soirée, complete with burlesque singers, flapper dancers, and jazz artists, transported guests into a decadent era of glamour and abandon. The night spilt into an afterparty that spun through the decades into a glittering disco, with each beat and smile captured forever in frames that P.Taufiq Photography so intuitively immortalised. Such is the power of great pictures—they are the ultimate keepsakes for posterity. Reminding us, every once in a while, that maybe everything does happen for a reason.

What started as an accidental squad addition evolved into a partnership, both in-game and off-screen. Tanupreet considered himself a professional gamer, and he was in no mood to play with a rookie. When a mutual friend added Jaspreet to a game, she was exactly that, still finding her bearings in the game. The story started off with a cliche, the classic enemies to lovers trope playing out. Tanupreet wasn’t particularly thrilled to have to play with Jaspreet. This changed over time and love blossomed. Their squad sessions turned into duo games, where shared tactics and quirks laid the foundation for something deeper. From Jaspreet’s playful map explorations to Tanupreet’s protecting her in the game, their connection blossomed—what began with a parachute drop in Pochinki, a place in the game, culminated in a love story. Blending tradition with technology, BGMI decided to recreate an Indian wedding for this unique couple inside the game, synchronised with their real-world ceremony. The digital festivities mirrored conventional celebrations, including a virtual One of the most important aspects of an Indian wedding are the ensembles. To reflect the ceremonial significance, the bride and groom’s virtual avatars were dressed in custom outfits co-designed by fashion designer Ritu Beri. The garments combined traditional Indian silhouettes with visual cues inspired by BGMI skins, offering a modern yet culturally grounded visual identity for the couple’s in-game avatars. This initiative was part of BGMI’s effort to highlight the real human stories emerging from its digital battlegrounds. “BGMI has been the starting point of so many beautiful relationships. In order to win a match in-game, you have to work together in heightened emotions, so you end up building bonds for a lifetime.
