article_title: How to ace your maid of honour duties—both before and during the wedding
sub_title: Yes, the role comes with some pressure but being asked to be a maid of honour is a sign that you are the bride’s number-one person
article_content: As the leader of the bridal party, there’s no denying that maid of honour duties are an important responsibility. If asked to take on the position, this best friend or close relative of the bride will be in charge of keeping the Yes, the role comes with some pressure—but being asked to be a maid (or man, or person) of honour is an incredible gesture and sign that you are the number-one person that your While the maid of honour’s level of involvement can vary based on how much the The maid of honour is a role designated by the bride as the leader of the bridal party. If the maid of honour is married, you could call them a “matron of honour” instead. Most often, the So what responsibilities fall into the maid of honour’s to-do list before the wedding even takes place? Ahead we break down the key parts of a MOH’s role ahead of the wedding. The most important role of a maid of honour is to be a right hand to the bride. Wedding planning is an exciting time, but it also can occasionally feel like a full-time job. It’s also a period where a couple could be having important The maid of honour is pretty much the camp counsellor of the bridal party. As the leader of the pack, you will ensure everyone is well informed of any and all plans. You will craft group emails and text messages, create itineraries for the bachelorette and wedding day, and answer the necessary questions that the bride doesn’t have to be burdened with. It’s a good idea to collect all wedding party member’s contact info from the bride as soon as you say “yes” to the job so you can get on top of coordination. Be warned that your role as lead communicator might have to come down to working out any conflicts within the group as well. The bachelorette party is likely the biggest undertaking a maid of honour will take. If the bride decides to do a destination trip, you will likely be charged with securing a hotel or Airbnb, organising activities, making reservations, creating a budget and getting payments from the attendees. Throughout the event, you should play check-in frequently to make sure the plans are running smoothly and the bride is having a great time. While you might be the leader of the event, it’s totally fine (and encouraged for your own wellbeing) to delegate and collaborate with other bridal party members to bring plans to life. Traditionally, the maid of honour would also take charge of planning the bridal shower. Today, that isn’t necessarily the case. While a MOH can still host the bridal shower, a close family member or multiple people in the bridal party may offer to plan the event, too. This party is all about “showering” a bride with gifts while surrounded by close friends and female family members. If you are hosting, it’s important to find a great venue, send invitations, supply food and drinks, curate decorations and organise fun activities for the guests. You also should help lead the gift-giving part of the event and keep the list of presents organised so the bride can easily write thank-you notes later. Once the bride decides their vision for the wedding party attire, the maid of honour should help to make sure the bridal party all gets appropriate looks. Many wedding parties don’t all wear the exact same dress anymore, so it’s a good idea to work with the bride to send an email with all the details of outfit guidelines, providing timelines needed for orders or approvals, and follow up to ensure everyone has their ensembles ready in time for the big day. Once the wedding day arrives, a maid of honour will need to kick into high gear to take on these important tasks. There are lots of moving parts on a wedding day, from getting hair and makeup done to taking photos to walking down the aisle. A maid of honour should be there to help corral the bridal party to make it to every event in a timely manner. The morning of a wedding can be a fun and meaningful time for the bridal party as they all get ready for the big day. The maid of honour should make sure this space is well prepared with food, water, and maybe a little champagne for everyone to enjoy as they get glammed up and prepare for the long day ahead. The bride should have a relaxing wedding day—and not be the person fielding questions from a wedding planner or confused guests. The maid of honour will help with those last coordinating details and relay any necessary information to the wedding party. It’s a good idea to get contact info of the wedding planners or venue coordinators before the day of so you can be in communication at all times. It’s perfectly normal for a bride who’s distracted by all the moving parts to forget about eating enough during the day or get some jitters. A maid of honour should be on top of ensuring the bride always has food and water available, as well as being a shoulder for them to lean on if they need to talk through any nerves. During the ceremony, a bride will traditionally hand off the bouquet to the maid of honour for important moments like vows and exchanging rings. In addition to the floral arrangement, a maid of honour may be asked to hold onto items for the bride like lipstick, a cell phone, or a speech. It’s a good idea to keep a clutch with you or choose an outfit with pockets for this purpose. You might also need to join the bride in the bathroom if their large lehenga needs to be strategically held when they’re relieving themselves. At the reception, you might also be needed to take the gift envelopes received by the couple to a place for safekeeping. Traditionally, the maid of honour is one of the few guests who give a speech at the wedding reception. It’s best to make this speech sweet, sentimental, and a bit funny, if that’s your forté. Make sure to pre-write your speech and practise if you can so you don’t let nerves take hold. Also, be sure to keep it on the shorter side so everyone can have plenty of time later on the dance floor. While you absolutely can enjoy the specialty cocktails and get down on the dance floor, it’s best for the maid of honour not to go overboard. Feel free to keep your energy up and have fun alongside the bride all night, but remember that you should still be a helpful presence rather than someone who needs help. If there’s a day-after party, you will want to be in good shape to help the bride with any last needs.

article_title: Inside a Jaipur couple’s grand wedding in Rajasthan’s Aravalli Hills
sub_title: Arpit and Khushboo’s wedding ceremony at DoubleTree by Hilton Jaipur Amer blended their love story with immersive experiences for guests
article_content: For Arpit Parwal and Khushboo Choraria, love first sparked in the corridors of their high school in Jaipur. What started as a teenage friendship turned into a lifelong bond, one that endured distance, time zones, and countless video calls. “On Valentine’s Day in 10th grade, Khushboo got down on one knee in the middle of the school grounds and asked me to be her Valentine,” Arpit recalls. “That moment set the course for everything that followed.” Even as life (and their careers) initially took them to different cities, Arpit works as a software engineer in Seattle, USA, while Khushboo has now launched her own custom gifting and jewellery brand, their connection remained unbreakable. “Despite the miles, we always found our way back to each other,” they share. So, when it came to their wedding, they knew it had to be a celebration of their story—a blend of grand gestures and intimate, thoughtful details. For the Jaipur natives, a local wedding venue that still felt like a destination was key. “We wanted something scenic, luxurious, and easily accessible for our guests,” Khushboo explains. DoubleTree by Hilton Jaipur Amer, nestled against the Aravalli Hills, offered the perfect mix of breathtaking views and seamless hospitality. “Beyond the stunning location, it was Hilton’s expertise in hosting large-scale weddings that sealed the deal,” Arpit shares. The hotel’s Wedding Ambassador worked closely with us from day one, helping us craft a stress-free experience that allowed us to focus on enjoying our celebrations. For Arpit and Khushboo, their wedding wasn’t just about them—it was about making their family and friends feel truly special and welcomed. Thoughtful gestures were incorporated right from the time guests arrived, until their departure. For instance, welcome hampers were stocked with the couple’s favourite snacks with personal notes explaining why each item was chosen. A custom radio show played in cars that ferried guests from the airport, sharing stories about the couple’s journey, while room keys were handed in the form of a ‘Book of Love’, that doubled as a keepsake, complete with the wedding itinerary and tiny, personalised elements. Another feature that was a hit with guests was a live wedding magazine updated via their Instagram handle, that ensured guests felt part of the journey, weeks before the celebrations began. “Hilton’s Wedding Ambassador made sure every touchpoint was executed perfectly,” Khushboo shares. “From coordinating the guest arrivals to handling last-minute changes, they were our support system.” Each event was themed around a chapter of their love story. So, the welcome party was themed as an ‘Around the World’ carnival—a nod to their shared love for travel, featuring favourite dishes from places they visited together. The after-party was inspired by an airport lounge, thanks to the years of long-distance travel that the couple undertook, along with personalised boarding pass invitations. Menus were tailored for each event, from an authentic Rajasthani feast at the bhaat ceremony to a global gourmet spread reflecting their travels. "We worked closely with Hilton’s F&B team to ensure every dish felt intentional," Arpit adds. One of the most emotional moments came during the sangeet, as the couple exchanged rings while over 40 of their closest friends cheered them on. “Seeing that love and support from our people, it was overwhelming in the best way,” Arpit recalls. As the wedding celebrations unfolded under the Jaipur night sky, guests were treated to a spectacular sufi performance, fireworks, and an evening of dance and revelry. “Thanks to Hilton’s Wedding Ambassador and the team, we were able to fully immerse ourselves in the joy of our wedding, without worrying about a thing.” For the couple, their wedding was a celebration of their story, their journey, and the people who made it special. "As the sky turned an inky blue and we toasted to our new life together, we knew one thing for sure—this was exactly how we had imagined it," they share.

article_title: The bridal hair trends defining 2025
sub_title: L’Oréal Professionnel is making a case for timeless bridal hair, with deep mocha hues, ultra-luxe shine and scalp-first care routines that start long before the wedding day
article_content: A wedding is no place for half-measures—least of all when it comes to hair. This season, the trends are steeped in intention and rooted in care. It’s not about passing fads that come in one day and fade out by the next, but about a look that feels like you, only amplified. From the return of deep, luxurious brunettes to the sharp, considered cut that needs no embellishment—this is hair for the bride who knows exactly who she is. Forget fleeting shades. This year, depth is everything. Pantone’s Mocha Mousse sets the tone—rich, dimensional, with an elegance that never competes. Brown is far from basic and L’Oréal Professionnel is ensuring that every bride finds her perfect version of it. The secret? A virtual try-on that lets you refine your shade before committing. The aim is clear: choose a tone that complements your natural beauty, setting a refined backdrop for your bridal look. There’s beauty in precision and 2025 brides aren’t hiding behind excessive layers or cascading curls. Instead, they’re opting for clean, decisive cuts that let hair fall exactly as it should—no fuss, no excess. A straight, sculpted bob or a well-balanced length that moves effortlessly. The rule? The simpler the cut, the greater the impact. It’s an approach that celebrates restraint—crafted with clarity and a deep understanding of your unique style. Shine is having its moment—not the artificial, lacquered kind but the kind that speaks of deeply nourished, impossibly healthy hair. Inspired by the Korean glass skin trend, this is about high-gloss, weightless fluidity. The trick? A routine that starts long before the wedding: bi-monthly L’Oréal Professionnel Hair Spa sessions, a targeted scalp diagnosis, and the Absolut Repair 10-in-1 oil to seal in the glow. It is care with purpose, producing a mirror-like effect that speaks to genuine attention. Long hair, undone but intentional. There’s a shift towards softness, a rejection of overworked updos in favour of strands that flow freely. But effortless never means unprepared. To wear hair loose on your wedding day is to commit to months of care with a dedicated routine—comprising a gentle shampoo, restorative mask, and a targeted serum—ensures that your hair remains resilient and vibrant, ready to frame your day with subtle power. sub_title: Arjun Kartha, founder of Twogether Studios and Prabhjot Kaur, Hilton Wedding Ambassador, share expert tips for couples for capturing those precious wedding memories on film
article_content: Weddings are a magical blend of love, laughter, memories and shared traditions. From the time you gather with your family and friends, walk down the aisle and share stolen glances with your significant other, to toasting to a lifetime together—all combined in a vibrant celebration—it’s these little moments that make any wedding a standout affair. And it’s only fitting that these precious moments be captured on camera so you can look back on them fondly, no matter how much time has passed by. However, finding the right photography team or studio for your dream wedding is easier said than done. You want to be able to work with a team that understands your vision, who you are as a couple, and the kind of photography you’re both looking for— whether moody, cinematic, editorial or taking the much-loved storytelling approach. Arjun Kartha, founder of Delhi-based Twogether Studios which has been a leading name in wedding photography and cinematography for the past decade, and Prabhjot Kaur, Hilton Wedding Ambassador, take us through According to Kartha, one of the key factors to pulling off a dream wedding is setting aside enough time to capture moments on film. Couples often tend to overlook this small but significant step that allows them to capture those fleeting but heartwarming moments. “Instead of squeezing multiple events into a single day, consider spacing them out, so the team has enough room to capture those meaningful moments—like your couple portraits, family group shots and candid interactions—without feeling too rushed,” he suggests. Kartha can’t emphasise enough on the importance of sketching out a brief for your photography studio. How about putting together a mood board for them to reference? According to him, this kind of visual inspiration is invaluable. “For example, Pinterest boards are a great way to convey this,” he explains, adding that this helps the photographer to understand your aesthetic and preferences—whether you’re drawn to soft, pastel hues, bold pops of color, sleek modern lines, or even classic, timeless looks. He cautions that it’s also important to keep your expectations realistic. “For instance, if you’re having a night wedding, your inspiration shouldn’t be drawn from daytime functions.” Equally important is clarity around what you don’t want, he adds. “Lean into what your vibe is as a couple and allow that to be front and centre of your story,” suggests Prabhjot Kaur, Hilton Wedding Ambassador. Personalisation is key here, as you can add several tiny details to your wedding celebrations that will reflect your story and journey. She recalls working with a bride recently who wanted to embroider her husband’s name onto her wedding saree, making for a heartfelt keepsake. According to Kaur, what matters beyond curating the perfect decor, a great food spread and the right dose of entertainment, is crafting meaningful moments that reflect your story, which will ultimately translate on film. This could be anything from personalising your wedding ceremony set-up that is unique to your family’s traditions or focusing on who you both are by bringing your own ideas and thoughts to the table. “Share as many details and ideas that you have in mind, and we’ll work towards making it happen,” she says. Kaur adds that as wedding ambassadors, the team and the hotel are always available at hand to help couples with the best photo-friendly locations, capture the perfect shot for the gram, and even work behind the scenes with the photographers to ensure its smooth sailing on your big day. While trends in the wedding space can be fleeting, they can also work in elevating your wedding photos and film. Kartha believes that storytelling and authenticity are definitely at the forefront of wedding photography at the moment. “Couples increasingly want their images to feel like a true reflection of who they are, rather than a series of staged moments. This means focusing on interactions, raw emotions, and capturing the atmosphere and energy of the celebration as it naturally unfolds.” This also allows wedding photography to serve both as art and memory—with gorgeous, evocative imagery that showcases the couple’s story.

article_title: Why this couple chose a magical riverfront wedding at DoubleTree by Hilton Goa-Panaji over the beach

article_content: Most couples who choose Goa for a destination wedding, do so with the expectation of having a scenic beachfront wedding, complete with sunset pheras and fireworks thrown in for good measure. Tanya Sharma and Tarun Makhijani decided otherwise, choosing to skip the classic beach wedding for a quaint riverfront setting at the DoubleTree by Hilton Goa-Panaji. Goa held a special place in their heart—it’s where their love story began, as Tarun, a well-known wedding and club DJ, and Tanya first met at a celebration there. “We were introduced by common friends and spoke briefly. We didn’t think much of it, carrying on with our lives. It was only in 2020 during the lockdown when he reached out via text and we started talking,” Sharma reveals. Their worlds might have been far apart—Tanya works as an independent sports consultant, while Tarun is a wedding and club DJ—however fate had its way and four years later, they decided to seal their love in a surreal celebration surrounded by their closest family and friends—back where it all began. The couple knew they wanted to host their nuptials in Goa, but a beach wedding wasn’t on the cards. Instead, they started looking for one-off venues that retained Goa’s charm and offered a different take on the sunshine state. A visit to the DoubleTree by Hilton Goa- Panaji, ticked all the boxes for the couple and their families, with its quaint location in the capital city, scenic river views and distant hills framing the backdrop. DoubleTree by Hilton Goa-Panaji offers breathtaking vistas of lush hills and winding waters, paired with modern luxury across its 160 elegant rooms and suites. Nestled on the banks of the winding Mandovi River with 160 rooms and suites, the resort offers unparalleled vistas set in the lap of nature. “We loved the fact that the resort had this gorgeous setting overlooking the river and the hills, and enough venue options for each of our celebrations,” they both share. The celebrations began with an intimate haldi ceremony in the alfresco area of a charming riverside restaurant, with vibrant marigold decor. This was followed by the mehendi in the bride’s suite clubbed with a private terrace. The next day, the infinity pool became the perfect venue for a lively sundowner featuring craft cocktails and fun games—an ideal setting to capture those gram-worthy shots and soak up the pleasant weather. Unbeknownst to Sharma, her beau had a surprise proposal planned for her at the pool party, where he went down on one knee and slipped a sparkling diamond ring on her finger, with their friends and family cheering them on. “Somehow, he managed to rope in our closest friends to pull off this surprise and sweep me off my feet,” Tanya reveals. The evening’s revelry continued with a grand sangeet and cocktail party in the resort’s expansive ballroom, known for its elegant design and ability to host lively celebrations. The couple were treated to special dance performances by their friends and family, as well as a live band that belted out several hits. The next day dawned bright and early with perfect weather, as the resort’s poolside venue underwent a transformation for the set-up of the wedding mandap. For Tanya, one of the most precious memories from their special day was when she walked down the aisle towards her beau. “I loved everything about my bridal entry. The fact that Tarun was in tears when he first saw me as a bride, was both emotional and beautiful at the same time,” she shares. As they took their pheras, with a dramatic sunset for company that painted the sky in vibrant hues, the love in the air was palpable. This was followed by a live sufi act and fireworks for a fitting finale. The celebrations ended with a reception and dinner in the ballroom with a curated F&B set-up for their guests to relish. “Every detail was thoughtfully curated, from my bridal entry to the custom menu. The team worked closely with us to infuse personal touches, like late-night snacks tailored for our post-dance cravings,” Tanya shares. “The F&B team ensured everything reflected our tastes, from indulgent local Goan dishes to a curated dessert station with our favourite treats,” they added, referring to how the hotel’s chefs personally sat down with them to curate menus, all the way from breakfast to midnight munchies, especially after the long nights of dancing and revelry. “Everything was planned with so much detail and love, and what made it all the more special was seeing our family and friends have such a fabulous time at our wedding,” they add. As the sky turned an inky blue, washing away the vibrant sunset hues, the couple toasted with glasses of champagne to a brand-new chapter in their lives, marking the perfect finale to their wedding celebrations.

article_title: How to write and deliver the best wedding speech
sub_title: Whether you’re the father of the bride, best man, or maid of honour, learn how to write—and deliver—the best wedding speech
article_content: If one of your nearest and dearest is tying the knot, it’s possible you may feel pressured to deliver the best A wedding speech presents a unique challenge: There’s no set formula for how the speech should play out, but it often requires sentimentality, a touch of humour and the good sense to know when to wrap it up. That’s why it’s pretty easy to overthink how Have you been asked to give a wedding toast at an upcoming celebration? There’s no reason to sweat. Instead, read ahead to learn how to write the best wedding speech and plan for your big moment. First off, it’s important to make sure that the couple definitely The to-be-weds also have the right to curate the day as they wish, and occasionally at a rehearsal dinner or welcome party, the couple may open the floor to additional toasts. But if this doesn’t happen, grabbing the mic unexpectedly for an off-the-cuff speech (especially after a few glasses of wine) will not be appreciated. If you are asked to give a toast, it’s important that you don’t just wing it. “First, recognise that speechwriting is a creative process,” shares Allison Shapira, founder and CEO of Global Public Speaking. “Give yourself plenty of time to be creative (i.e. not the night before, when you already have so much to stress about). Wait for your most creative time of the day, and turn off any distractions. Spend some unrushed time thinking about your relationship to the couple, and what you’d like to say.” While there’s no exact template to follow, there is a common basic formula to adhere to. “The framework I recommend for a wedding speech is: story, message, blessing,” Shapira shares. “Tell a heartwarming story, share the message or value behind that story, and then offer a blessing or wish for the couple based on that message.” “Typically, we advise our speakers to try to bring the audience on a journey where you initially try to make them laugh, then get to the real depth of the speech and earn some tears, then bring the whole speech full circle with a deep insight or story about the couple that ends with a funny final punch,” says Steven Greitzer, CEO and founder of Provenance, an AI company that specialises in helping write personalised wedding vows, ceremonies, and toasts. “It’s important to have a good balance of humour and sentimentality because, if it’s a full roast, it can feel like you’re just doing a standup comedy show for your own benefit and it could lack substance. Or, if it’s too overly emotional, it can get heavy and perhaps a bit too somber for a wedding celebration.” When choosing a story, Shapira recommends thinking carefully about who will be in the room. “It should obviously be good-natured, without making anyone look bad. And, it all depends on the family dynamics,” she says. “What one family considers good-natured, another family could consider scathing. Choose someone in the audience whom you think could give you some helpful feedback, and practise the speech with them in advance.” Greitzer adds that it’s important for both members of the couple to be highlighted in the speech. “Great anecdotes showcase who each person was before meeting, their synergy together, and their individual and collective growth,” he says. If you don’t know one member of the happy couple very well and are unfamiliar with their love story, don’t be afraid to get creative. “One of the best speeches I’ve seen was from a bridesmaid who hadn’t really been able to spend too much time with her best friend’s fiance because of the pandemic,” Greitzer shares. “She creatively read texts she found in her phone that gave her a hilarious timeline of her friend falling in love.” If you’re still not sure where to begin, consider giving an AI platform a try to help you form your toast. “The Provenance tools guide speakers to create unique, and personal ceremonies, vows, and toasts without the stress. It’s a partner in your brainstorming process; a way to help you verbalise what you were trying to say—but faster,” explains Greitzer. “Instead of being some outdated, mad-libs-style template, the expert-curated prompts inspire special stories and insights, ultimately weaving your responses together into a custom, editable first draft.” A final writing tip from Shapira? “I definitely recommend creating an outline but do not recommend writing the speech out word for word. When we script the entire speech, it sounds too formal,” says the public speaking expert. “I recommend first brainstorming the content, rearranging it into a logical structure, then drafting a general outline which you can bring with you to the event. While it may look better to simply give the speech ‘from the heart,’ the stress involved in trying to memorise your speech is simply not worth it.” The ideal length of a toast is between two to four minutes, which translates to around 500 to 1000 words on a page. Still, Greitzer notes, “The perfect length for the wedding toast complies with whatever length the couple wants it to be. Many guests don’t realise that long speeches can impact the whole evening’s timeline and affect the caterer, DJ, and so much more.” Best rule of thumb? Keep it short and sweet. Writing a wedding speech is half the battle—next comes your performance. It’s important that your toast has a good flow, feels natural, and doesn’t drag on. Here’s where the idiom “practice makes perfect” rings true. Shapira advises giving yourself a few weeks of rehearsal to make your speech feel authentic and fluid. Her recommendations? “Read your speech out loud and make sure it stays within the time you have allotted. Read it to someone else and get their feedback. Record it and watch it back. We use a tool called AMPLIFY to get AI-based feedback.” She adds, “Don’t memorise the speech, but do read it out loud and make sure it sounds like your voice.” While it’s now common to see toasts being read off a phone, both experts agree that it’s much better to print out your speech. “Reading off of a phone comes with the risk of distractions from notifications, a weird backlight that can affect the colour of your face in photos, finicky technical difficulties, and having that annoying sound interference with the mic,” says Greitzer. (You also should make sure your speech is legible with a large font and wide spacing so you can easily find your place.) Watching yourself in front of a mirror can also be helpful to understand your body language during the performance. The final hurdle of giving a wedding toast is getting over your nerves. “Find a quiet place right beforehand to centre yourself (perhaps the bathroom or a corner of the room), pause and breathe, and remind yourself why you care about the couple,” recommends Shapira. She also adds—perhaps unsurprisingly—that it’s best to hold back on alcohol consumption ahead of the toast. You might think liquid courage can help you, but it’s best to not let yourself go a glass too far. “No one expects a perfect or professional speech; they want a unique, authentic message. The speech isn’t about you—it’s about the couple. Once you reframe the fact that the centre of attention isn’t on you, you can relax.”

article_content: If you’ve ever wondered how to say no to being a “I think one of the hard and fast rules is when this question gets asked of you is to ask about what the role entails. If imagining serving as a bridesmaid gives you When it comes to matrimonial commitments, financial transparency is key, says event and wedding planner Brianne Garritano, adding that weddings, and the cost of being a bridesmaid, are more complex nowadays. According to a study by If being a bridesmaid is outside of your current financial budget, you don’t have to go into debt just because you were asked. “It can be really, really hard,” shares Post. “You feel like you’re letting someone down, and yet at the same time, it’s their event, it’s not your event. If you’re worried about the financial and time commitment of pre-wedding events for the bridal party, Post reveals an etiquette rule that many might not know. “Bridesmaids are not required to go to any of those events—bachelorette party, showers, anything,” she shares. “What they are required to do is show up for the rehearsal, the ceremony and the reception. And if you’re in the unenviable position of having to decline the position, don’t waste any time telling the bride. “You should tell her right away, as soon as possible,” says event and wedding planner Mindy Weiss, adding that the conversation should take place in person when possible, and over the phone if not. article_title: Wedding invitation etiquette both couples and guests should follow
sub_title: An etiquette expert and wedding planner break down everything you need to know about wedding invitation rules
article_content: If you have a wedding on the horizon, a wedding invitation becomes the perfect vehicle to ensure that all your guests know all the ins and outs of your plans leading up to the big day. But since there are often From when to send your invitations to indicating whether guests can bring their kids, it’s best to have everything in place ahead of time so you can actually enjoy the process and have all your logistics set in stone. Ahead, an etiquette expert and wedding planner break down everything you need to know about wedding invitation rules. Get your guests excited for the wedding and have them mark their calendars with your save-the-dates. This invite usually has minimal details including the date and location of your event. “Save-the-dates are typically sent six to eight months before the wedding,” advises Myka Meier, best-selling author and founder of Beaumont Etiquette. “For The proper wedding invitations are usually a more thorough and formal correspondence that can include inserts, details of pre-wedding events and requests for RSVPs. “Wedding invitations should be sent out six to eight weeks before the big day,” advises Meier. “This allows your guests ample time to plan while ensuring the details are still fresh in their minds. For destination weddings, send invitations a bit earlier—ideally three months in advance.” To make logistics easier on your side, Gurl believes pushing this date out is best. “I like to advise my clients to send their invitations out 12 weeks before their wedding date with an RSVP by date six weeks before their wedding date,” she says. Guests should respond with their RSVPs promptly and within deadlines so couples don’t have to send out tedious follow-up emails and texts. We now live in a digital era, so many wonder if they should keep all their wedding correspondences online. “The choice between Of course, there’s still something special about a paper invitation. “We love physical paper...it is the first introduction into the look and feel of your day,” says Gurl. A great solution is a hybrid—sending an invite over paper and allowing more details to be given on the website. “We have been finding that more couples are choosing to RSVP online, which is a fast and easy way to track down guest count.” She adds, “Don’t worry—the older crowd is savvier than you think and can totally figure it out. If you are requesting mailed RSVPs, always include return postage. “It’s a thoughtful touch, makes it easier for guests to respond promptly and spares them the effort of finding or paying for a stamp,” says Meier. For a formal wedding, the response card can be written: “Kindly reply by [RSVP Date]. M________ will attend / will not attend.” For a more casual event: “RSVP by [Date]. [ ] Gladly accepts [ ] Regretfully unable to attend.” Much to many people’s surprise, there’s no set way you need to address your invites. You can either go formal and address couples as “Mr. and Mrs. John Smith,” or choose to write their full names. “This is totally up to the preferences of the couple and the vibe of the Planning out your ensembles for a wedding day can often require as much planning as booking a flight or finding accommodation. That’s why it’s important to include the dress code on your invitations. “The dress code should be placed at the bottom of the invitation—for example ‘ Once again, the wedding website is king when it comes to giving out more information. “Avoid including the registry directly on the invitation, as it can feel as if you are asking for a gift in order to attend and is therefore considered incorrect etiquette to do so,” shares Meier. “Instead, keep things polished by directing guests to your website.” Unless an invitation clearly states an invitee has a plus one or can bring “To indicate children aren’t invited, avoid writing ‘adults only’ on the invitation,” she notes. When a couple only has a certain capacity at their wedding If you do decide to have a second round of invites, Meier advises to proceed with caution. “If you’re waiting on first-round RSVPs before inviting others, ensure there’s enough time to send invitations and receive responses without making guests feel like an afterthought,” she says. “Digital invitations work well for the second group to streamline the process.”
